title: Investigate and remediate Helm preflight nodegroup orphaning causing tenant outages during on-prem upgrades
creator: Asha Patel
description: Several customers running Private/VPC on-prem upgrades observed their nodegroup controller leaving orphaned tenant NodeSets after the Helm preflight checks race. This causes API timeouts, operator reconcile loops, and customer-visible inference outages. This ticket owns the root cause investigation, immediate customer mitigations, and a surgical rollforward patch to prevent recurrence.
reproduction_steps: 1) Install operator-3.3.x in a staging 3-node cluster with tenant namespace and NodeSet replication enabled
2) Trigger an onprem upgrade that patches the operator Helm chart values with a simultaneous ConfigMap change applied via CI
3) Observe preflight hook ordering: preflight helm hook sometimes completes after the nodeagent manifests are applied leading to NodeSet label discrepancy
4) Operator reconcile detects missing NodeSet finalizers and attempts to recreate resources, leaving orphaned NodeSets and detached pods
investigation_summary: Initial triage showed a race between the Helm preflight Hook and the operator bootstrap reconciliation: the preflight removes an alpha annotation used by the operator to gate migration steps
Telemetry: controller logs (trace-id zyx-113) show repeated 409/404 during CR updates; metrics dashboard highlights spike in reconcile latency during window 02:12-02:18 UTC
Core cause hypothesis: Helm preflight hook executes a conditional CR update that strips tenant-identity labels when it runs before the new operator version's migration codepath is ready
Reproducer created in staging: scripts/repro/preflight-orphan-repro.sh (linked below).
impact_observations: Customer A (onprem): inference latency >3s and 15% request failures for 22 minutes
Customer B (VPC): operator enters crashloop on one replica leading to degraded HA for tenant orchestration
SLO exposure: paging threshold breached for dedicated-tenant control-plane for two customers
mitigation_taken: 1) Emergency: applied gateway-based traffic diversion to Hosted fallback for affected tenants (runbook step 4)
2) Safety patch: added a pre-upgrade webhook lock (temporary) to sequencer to avoid concurrent preflight changes
3) Customer communications: issued targeted incident notes and rollback instructions to SEs and CS team
action_items: A. Implement surgical rollforward that makes the Helm preflight idempotent: add explicit label-preserve logic and a coordination annotation
B. Add an operator-side migration guard: delay migration steps until a preflight-completion annotation is present (5m timeout)
C. Add e2e test that simulates concurrent Helm preflight + operator reconcile under high node churn
D. Create dashboard alert for preflight-timing-anomaly (metric: helm.preflight.duration) and reconcile-failure-rate
E. Update runbook: include automated safe-rollback to previous operator revision with staged drain of NodeSets
rollback_plan: If rollforward causes regression: perform immediate operator helm rollback to operator-3.3.9 via 'helm rollback' in tenant cluster
Restore backed-up CRs from s3://redwood-backups/onprem/preflight-336019 (last known-good at 2026-02-28T23:50:00Z)
Run reconciliation dry-run to validate NodeSet finalizer presence before reattaching workloads
deploy_plan: Canary rollout in internal staging cluster (1 tenant) with additional logging enabled
Progress to two external pilot customers (Customer C and Customer D) for 24h observation
If stable, roll to remaining onprem clusters with 10-minute staggered windows and health check gates
Post-deploy validation: no new orphaned NodeSets for 72h, reconcile latency within baseline
risks: Coordination annotation introduces another failure mode if Helm hooks run in unexpected order on older kubernetes versions
Delayed migration guard could increase upgrade timeouts for extremely large clusters; need conservative timeout defaults
Rollback involves CR restore; potential for transient mismatch in secret rotations
